crates.name: molla-solvers
crates.purpose_one_line: Time-domain dynamics backends: rigid-body integrators (Featherstone/CRBA/RNEA/XPBD/semi-implicit), soft-body descent (VBD), barrier-Newton contact, and particle/fluid solvers (MPM, implicit MPM, WCSPH).
main_modules: vbd.rs (2852) vertex block descent + Neo-Hookean tet blocks
barrier_solver.rs (718) Solver-trait wrapper over barrier oracle
sph_oracle.rs (808) f64 CPU oracle for SPH

crates.name: molla-fem
crates.purpose_one_line: Spatial discretisation: a full FEM toolbox (mesh/quadrature/element/assembly, P1/P2/Nedelec/DG spaces, elasticity + hyperelastic element kernels) plus the PDE solvers layered on it (Poisson/heat/wave/Stokes/NS/eddy-current/magnetostatics/phase-field/AMR/adjoint) and their GPU ports.
main_modules: signorini.rs (1952) Lagrange-multiplier hard contact + Coulomb friction + PDAS

overlap_verdicts.solvers_evidence: crates/molla-solvers/src/vbd.rs:1897 `neo_hookean_vertex_block` — analytic first Piola stress `P = μ·F + s·cof(F)` (vbd.rs:1970-1973), analytic per-vertex 3x3 Hessian block (vbd.rs:2030-2040), plus the Kelly-Bettis plastic return mapping and the F = Fe·Fp multiplicative split (vbd.rs:1922-1954). Evaluated per-vertex inside a descent loop.
overlap_verdicts.fem_evidence: crates/molla-fem/src/element.rs:765 `compute_element_neo_hookean_force` = `finite_difference_hyperelastic_force(...)` and :780 `..._tangent` = `finite_difference_hyperelastic_tangent(...)`; the energy at element.rs:708 is the SAME `0.5·μ(I1-3) - μ lnJ + 0.5·λ ln²J`. Mooney-Rivlin at element.rs:794/809 has the same FD structure.
overlap_verdicts.verdict: SAME CONSTITUTIVE LAW, DIFFERENT SIMULATION MODEL — keep separate. VBD is an analytic Hessian-based vertex-descent solver with plasticity; the FEM copy is a per-element assembly kernel whose force and tangent are computed by CENTRAL FINITE DIFFERENCES of the energy. They are not mergeable as solvers, but the shared energy density is a genuine duplication: FEM's FD tangent is ~9 extra energy evaluations per element per Newton iteration where VBD already has the closed form. Reuse candidate: one shared `neo_hookean_energy(F, mu, lam)` + the analytic tangent, with FEM keeping only its assembly scatter.
overlap_verdicts.risk: medium — merging kernels touches VBD's tested SPD guarantees; extract the energy/tangent, do not merge the solvers

overlap_verdicts.solvers_evidence: barrier_contact.rs:1-28 — damped Newton with a CCD-truncated line search on the IPC incremental potential, matrix-free PCG inner solve, min_gap invariant asserted every step. Also ik.rs (LM + L-BFGS), implicit_mpm.rs (colored Gauss-Seidel, no Newton).
overlap_verdicts.fem_evidence: solver.rs:1656 `solve_nonlinear_static`, solver.rs:1825 `solve_distortion_minimization`, signorini.rs:1308 `solve_active_set_signorini` (PDAS Newton outer loop), eddy_current.rs (`gmres_with_precond`), stokes.rs Uzawa-CG outer loop.
overlap_verdicts.verdict: DIFFERENT PROBLEMS SHARING THE NAME — keep separate, improve naming. The solved systems are disjoint: solvers' Newton minimises a soft-body incremental potential over particle positions (n = 3·particles); fem's Newton iterates a Lagrange-multiplier saddle-point for hard contact or a nonlinear FE residual (n = DoFs). Neither can call the other. Naming improvement: `barrier_contact::Newton` → `barrier_newton_potential`; `signorini::solve_active_set_signorini` → `contact_newton_pdas`.

overlap_verdicts.solvers_evidence: (a) barrier_contact.rs:1-28 IPC cubic compact-support barrier, analytic half-space + sphere obstacles (phase 1, no VT/EE). (b) vbd_soft_contact.rs:1-28 VT + EE cross-mesh contact via `crate::geometry::SoftBvh`, emitting VtContact/EeContact for VBD. (c) xpbd.rs:1-10 position-projection contacts.
overlap_verdicts.fem_evidence: (a) signorini.rs:1-60 Lagrange-multiplier hard non-penetration, Coulomb friction projected onto a disc of radius μλn, PDAS outer loop; candidates come from the SHARED geometry layer — signorini.rs:124 `use crate::geometry::SelfContactCandidate` and :1154 `signorini_candidates_from_self_contacts`. (b) bc.rs Dirichlet/Neumann/Nitsche (`default_nitsche_sigma`). (c) nonconforming.rs penalty contact via `molla_geometry::{TetAabb, TetBvh}` (nonconforming.rs:94).
overlap_verdicts.verdict: THREE DIFFERENT CONTACT FORMULATIONS, one shared broad phase — keep separate. Barrier (soft, always-feasible), Signorini/PDAS (hard, exact constraints, friction cone), penalty (soft nonconforming) are textbook-distinct and have different convergence guarantees; the code says so explicitly in each header. The real duplication is upstream: BOTH get candidate pairs from `molla-geometry`, which is correct and worth keeping. Merge candidate: none of the three, but the barrier and Signorini paths both invent their own matrix-free Krylov inner loop.
overlap_verdicts.risk: low — correctly separated today; do not merge

overlap_verdicts.solvers_evidence: No CPU Krylov implementation in solvers — it calls `molla_math`. barrier_contact.rs:29-30 notes 'matrix-free PCG'; sph_oracle/sph_diff are explicit. GPU paths live in `molla-kernels` (`bsr_cg_gpu` bsr_solve.rs:27, `bsr_gmres_gpu` bsr_solve.rs:138).
overlap_verdicts.fem_evidence: solver.rs:29 `use crate::math::iterative::{CgResult, JacobiPreconditioner, cg_solve, pcg_solve}` with call sites at solver.rs:177,208,291,332 — the SHARED CPU implementation. fem ALSO ships its own 3873-line GPU Krylov stack in gpu_kernels/fem_cg.rs: `cg_solve_resident` (:614), `cg_solve_resident_lazy` (:794), `cg_solve_resident_lazy_prepared` (:950), `cg_solve_resident_fused` (:1152), `pcg_solve_resident` (:1325), `read_buffer` (:1491) — and its doc comments explicitly claim parity with `crate::math::iterative::CgResult` (:613) and `pcg_solve` (:1323).
overlap_verdicts.verdict: REAL DUPLICATION on the GPU side — mergeable. The CPU side is already correctly shared through `molla-math`. But `molla-fem`'s `FemCgGpuKernel` is a private reimplementation of the same CG/PCG that `molla-kernels::bsr_solve.rs` (`bsr_cg_gpu`) already provides on the same `BsrGpu` type that fem_cg.rs:1155/2845 itself imports from `crate::kernels`. Two GPU CG implementations over one BSR type in one workspace.
overlap_verdicts.risk: high — merging needs a benchmark to prove the fem variant's fused/lazy paths are not faster; do not delete blind

overlap_verdicts.concept: Particle and fluid methods (MPM / SPH / APIC / Stokes / FFT)
overlap_verdicts.solvers_evidence: mpm.rs GPU granular MPM with APIC affine matrix C and affine damping (mpm.rs:63,186-187) — no FEM mesh involved. implicit_mpm.rs:488 CPU implicit MPM with Bingham rheology, colored Gauss-Seidel, no FEM. sph.rs GPU WCSPH; sph_oracle.rs f64 CPU oracle for the same WGSL math; sph_diff.rs differentiable SPH.
overlap_verdicts.fem_evidence: apic_coupling.rs:1-40 DEPOSITS MPM particles onto a P1 tet mesh via barycentric weights, then does a viscous Laplacian smoothing pass as an explicit v1 stand-in for a Stokes projection (apic_coupling.rs:28-40 admits this). stokes.rs Taylor-Hood P2/P1 + Uzawa-CG. fft_ns.rs FFT-Poisson fractional-step NS, documented at fft_ns.rs:4-6 as 'complementary' to the Taylor-Hood solver. stam_fluid.rs Stam stable fluids. multiphase.rs CSF/level-set. NO SPH anywhere in fem.
overlap_verdicts.verdict: SAME PHYSICS, THREE DISJOINT DISCRETISATIONS — keep separate, one naming fix. MPM appears twice: solvers owns the particle→grid GPU MPM (mpm.rs) while fem owns the particle→FEM-mesh APIC hybrid (apic_coupling.rs), which is a different transfer operator (mesh nodes vs background grid) and is documented as an MPM/FEM bridge, not a duplicate. SPH is solvers-only. Stokes/FFT/Stam/multiphase are fem-only. Fluid is therefore NOT redundant: solvers has Lagrangian particle fluids, fem has Eulerian grid fluids. Naming fix: `apic_coupling` → `mpm_fem_hybrid` so it does not read as a second MPM.
overlap_verdicts.risk: low — but note fem's APIC viscosity pass is a placeholder for a real Stokes projection and its own docs say so (apic_coupling.rs:28-40)

redundancy.summary: The two crates are siblings, not a stack, and they do not solve one problem twice. solvers is a time-domain dynamics library (particles, rigid chains, soft descent); fem is a spatial-discretisation library (mesh, elements, PDE solvers). The quantified overlaps reduce to two real code duplications and one shared formula.
real_duplications: molla-fem/src/gpu_kernels/fem_cg.rs (3873 loc) reimplements the CG/PCG that molla-kernels/src/bsr_solve.rs:27,138 already ships over the same BsrGpu type
Neo-Hookean energy appears analytically in solvers/src/vbd.rs:1897 and by finite differences in fem/src/element.rs:765,780
shared_by_design: CPU Krylov: both route through molla-math/src/iterative.rs (cg_solve:155, pcg_solve:247, bicgstab_solve:361)
Contact candidates: both route through molla-geometry (SoftBvh for solvers' vbd_soft_contact.rs:26; SelfContactCandidate/TetBvh for fem's signorini.rs:124, nonconforming.rs:94)
not_redundant: Contact: barrier vs Signorini/PDAS vs penalty are three distinct formulations
Newton: potential minimisation over particles vs saddle-point/residual over DoFs

connection_health.fan_out: Both crates are leaves with respect to each other (zero mutual edges) and both depend on the same six internal crates: molla-core, molla-math, molla-sim, molla-geometry, molla-storage, molla-kernels/compute. That shared substrate is where the actual coupling lives.
connection_health.facade: crates/molla/src/fem/mod.rs:6 is a single `pub use molla_fem::*` and crates/molla/src/solvers/mod.rs re-exports solvers per-module. Both are wired, both are exercised.
connection_health.viewer: The viewer reaches solvers through main.rs:61 and fem through main.rs:53 plus 19 examples. solvers' engines are all driven live (xpbdd/featherstone/vbd/barrier GPU ctor sites at main.rs:3534-3557, 3863, 4007, 11199). So neither crate is orphaned.
connection_health.asymmetry: fem exports roughly 4x as many symbols as solvers (lib.rs:120-245 is a ~125-line re-export wall) and a large minority are reachable only from its own tests. solvers' public surface is tight and almost entirely viewer-live.
connection_health.risk: the risk is not disconnection, it is over-export: fem's blanket `pub use` plus the facade's `pub use molla_fem::*` means every internal experiment is a public API commitment.
